title: Nested monomorphic inclusions of totalized smart vertical cutoffs
statement: Let C be abelian and suppose diagonal totals exist for every nonnegative double complex. For K, extend each vertical column by zero to the integers. The cutoff b is its smart truncation at b-1, restricted back to the nonnegative integers, totalized, then extended by zero. The top term is the similarly totalized extension-restriction of K and the bottom term is zero. Each canonical inclusion into the top term is monomorphic, and whenever i<=j the inclusion of term i factors through that of term j. This constructs the actual tower underlying [lem-sp-double-complex-vertical-spectral-object]; the smart window convention is [def-sp-double-complex-vertical-window].

source.place: Proof steps 1 and 2, first sequence: Nested monomorphic inclusions of totalized smart vertical cutoffs

proof.text: Canonical smart truncation inclusions are degreewise monomorphisms (kernels at the boundary, identities below, zero sources above). Restriction and extension preserve them. Every total degree has a finite diagonal, so finite biproducts preserve these monomorphisms.

For a<=b, truncate the a-cutoff at b-1: its truncation inclusion is an isomorphism, since it already has strict upper support a-1. Invert this inclusion and then apply truncation to the a-inclusion into the original column. Naturality gives a natural transformation from the a-cutoff to the b-cutoff, whose composite with the b-inclusion is the a-inclusion.

Apply the natural transformation columnwise, totalize and extend. At bottom use the zero map; at top use the identity. The factorization equation follows from functoriality. Monicity gives uniqueness and thus the functor laws for verticalTower.
